findings.problem: hT56 and hT13 are the same argument with the two components exchanged. In both, α ∈ S gives w • permLattice e6Rho (w₁⁻¹ • α) in the double image of S. The image equation hex2 or hex1 then rewrites that membership, and a preimage γ is extracted. Finally T α is recovered by `rw [← hγeq, smul_inv_smul]`. The ~11-line block is copied verbatim, and only the hypothesis (hex1 or hex2) and the support sets differ. It is nontrivial image-chasing, and any fix to one copy has to be mirrored in the other.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a small lemma before twoA2_graph_contra:

theorem weyl_lattice_image_mem {S S' : Set (Fin Tag.E6.rank → ℤ)} (w₁ w : WeylGroup Tag.E6)
    (hex : (fun x => w • permLattice e6Rho x) '' ((fun x => w₁⁻¹ • x) '' S) = (fun x => w₁⁻¹ • x) '' S')
    {α} (hα : α ∈ S) : w₁ • (w • permLattice e6Rho (w₁⁻¹ • α)) ∈ S'.

Proof sketch: `have h1 : w • permLattice e6Rho (w₁⁻¹ • α) ∈ (fun x => w • permLattice e6Rho x) '' ((fun x => w₁⁻¹ • x) '' S) := ⟨w₁⁻¹ • α, ⟨α, hα, rfl⟩, rfl⟩`, then `rw [hex] at h1`, `obtain ⟨γ, hγ, hγeq⟩ := h1`, `rw [← hγeq, smul_inv_smul]; exact hγ`.

Then hT56 becomes `fun α hα => weyl_lattice_image_mem w₁ w hex2 hα`, and hT13 becomes `fun α hα => weyl_lattice_image_mem w₁ w hex1 hα`. The expected types match those in the file. T unfolds definitionally to w₁ • (w • permLattice e6Rho (w₁⁻¹ • ·)), and support13/56 are defeq to supp13/56 as the current `⟨α, hα, rfl⟩` already relies on. Add `show` or `change` if elaboration needs it.
findings.benefit: The image-chasing argument is stated and proved once, and its symmetric use for the two A2 components is explicit. This shortens the already very long main proof by about 20 lines and removes the risk of the two copies diverging.

findings.problem: The two branches of `rcases hform` repeat the same proof skeleton. The first part is the root-permutation hypothesis, `fun i j hij t => by have h := hshape i j hij t; rw [(hπ i j).1, (hπ i j).2] at h; rw [RingHom.id_apply]; exact h`. The second is the hGLN proof (`Units.ext`, `coe_GL_coe_matrix`, `hA₀ X`, `Units.val_mul`, simp). The third is the discrepancy tail (`obtain ⟨z,hzZ,hz⟩ := hdisc A`, two `generalize`s, `simp only [map_mul, map_inv, hGLN] at hz`, `convert hz using 1`, `group`). The branches differ only by the lemma used (pos/neg) and by whether invTransposeHom is applied. This is nontrivial matrix and group reasoning that is maintained twice.
findings.proposed_change: Split out the shared interface rather than copying it. For example, add a lemma that, from `hdisc` and an equation `∀ X, toGL (N X) = A₀ * φ (toGL X) * A₀⁻¹` (φ = id or invTransposeHom), produces the hypothesis that not_twisted_discrepancy_pos/neg expect. In the file, the tail would be proved generically over a monoid hom φ : GL → GL, replacing the two `generalize … convert hz using 1; group` blocks. Also make the `hshape` rewrite a single local `have hroot : ∀ i j hij t, …` before the `rcases`, since it is identical in both branches. I have not verified that this generic form typechecks. The `simp`/`group` steps may need adjusting for each φ.
findings.benefit: The pos and neg cases would differ only in which exchange lemma and which discrepancy lemma they call. A reader could then see that the cases are structurally parallel, and the group-theoretic cleanup would not have to be fixed twice.
